requirements.heading: Best Practices for Submission Operation
requirements.text: If external submissions are supported -- that is, from outside a site's administrative domain -- then the domain's MSAs MUST support the SUBMISSION port 587 [RFC4409].

requirements.heading: Best Practices for Submission Operation
requirements.text: Operators MAY standardize on the SUBMISSION port for both external AND LOCAL users; this can significantly simplify submission operations.

requirements.heading: Best Practices for Submission Operation
requirements.text: MUAs SHOULD use the SUBMISSION port for message submission.

requirements.heading: Best Practices for Submission Operation
requirements.text: MSAs MUST perform authentication on the identity asserted during all mail transactions on the SUBMISSION port, even for a message having a RCPT TO address that would not cause the message to be relayed outside of the local administrative domain.

requirements.heading: Best Practices for Submission Operation
requirements.text: An operator of an MSA MUST ensure that the authenticated identity is authorized to submit email, based on an existing relationship between the submitting entity and the operator.

requirements.heading: Best Practices for Submission Operation
requirements.text: For a reasonable period of time after submission, the message SHOULD be traceable by the MSA operator to the authenticated identity of the user who sent the message.

requirements.heading: Transitioning to Submission Port
requirements.text: In order to promote transition of initial message submission from port 25 to port 587, MSAs MUST listen on port 587 by default and SHOULD have the ability to listen on other ports.

requirements.heading: Transitioning to Submission Port
requirements.text: MSAs MUST require authentication on port 587 and SHOULD require authentication on any other port used for submission.

requirements.heading: Transitioning to Submission Port
requirements.text: MSAs MAY also listen on other ports.

requirements.heading: Transitioning to Submission Port
requirements.text: Regardless of the ports on which messages are accepted, MSAs MUST NOT permit relaying of unauthenticated messages to other domains.

requirements.heading: Transitioning to Submission Port
requirements.text: As a default, MUAs SHOULD attempt to find the best possible submission port from a list of alternatives.

requirements.heading: Transitioning to Submission Port
requirements.text: The SUBMISSION port 587 SHOULD be placed first in the list.

requirements.heading: Transitioning to Submission Port
requirements.text: Since most MUAs available today do not permit falling back to alternate ports, sites SHOULD pre- configure or encourage their users to connect on the SUBMISSION port 587, assuming that site supports that port.

requirements.heading: Best Practices for Support of External Submissions
requirements.text: Access Providers MUST NOT block users from accessing the external Internet using the SUBMISSION port 587 [RFC4409].

requirements.heading: Best Practices for Support of External Submissions
requirements.text: When receiving email from outside their local operational environment, email service providers MUST distinguish between unauthenticated email addressed to local domains (MX traffic) versus submission-related authenticated email that can be addressed anywhere (MSA traffic).

requirements.heading: Message Submission Authentication/Authorization Technologies
requirements.text: Organizations SHOULD choose the most secure approaches that are practical.

requirements.heading: Message Submission Authentication/Authorization Technologies
requirements.text: It simply provides a warning that transmitting user credentials in clear text over insecure networks SHOULD be avoided in all scenarios as this could allow attackers to listen for this traffic and steal account data.

requirements.heading: Message Submission Authentication/Authorization Technologies
requirements.text: In these cases, it is strongly suggested that an appropriate security technology MUST be used.
